## D-040 — Two real-date checkpoints instead of simulated waves; checkpoint research layer
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("divide a year into 2 … randomly apply all the customer feedback into those two … if we know it for sure because it is posted on the internet, use realistic data … Jan 2026 and Jul 2026"; "forget everything we already implemented"), implemented by agent · Status: accepted for the research layer; how classification, clustering, contextualizing and requirement elicitation use it is left to Atahan's next steps · Supersedes D-027's wave definitions once integrated.
- Context: D-027 simulated time with a random 50/50 split plus an invented "market event" wave dated 2026-11 to 2027-11. Atahan questioned why waves exist at all and asked for real, dated public evidence so the effect of time on AI proposals is visible.
- Decision:
  1. **Two checkpoints** = what a PM could know on **31 Jan 2026** (FY2025 results) and **31 Jul 2026** (H1 2026 results). An item belongs to the earliest checkpoint whose cut-off is ≥ its source publication date; nothing published after 31 Jul 2026 is used. ## D-041 — Checkpoint lineage, comment galaxy and a new 3D frontend
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("design a black bg app with minimal design philosophy … graphic and 3D … make sure the second checkpoint will work on the output of checkpoint 1 and recalibrate requirements with the newly added data"; chose: comment galaxy as the first view, all BMW-internal data known at Jan, replace the old app, direction "track-while-scan"), implemented by agent · Status: accepted · Implements D-040; supersedes D-027's wave definitions and the D-039 screens.
- Decision:
  1. **Schema:** `checkpoint`, `checkpoint_run` (stage, parent_run_id), `track` (new/held/strengthened/weakened/lost with weight and prev_weight), `source_layout`; `source_item.checkpoint`. Module `bmw_req/checkpoints.py`: visibility rules, research import (`research/checkpoints/checkpoints.json` → `source_item(kind=research)`, 1,028 items), `start_run` refuses a cp2 run without a completed cp1 run of the same stage, `write_tracks` computes states against the parent and writes `lost` rows explicitly. Stage `acquire` run at both checkpoints (cp2: 6,645 held, 5,610 new). Tests: `tests/test_checkpoints.py`.
  2. **Galaxy:** all 10,128 raw comments embedded with text-embedding-3-small ($0.009) and laid out once in 3D (`bmw_req/pipeline/galaxy.py`); no AI interpretation of the text.
  3. **Frontend:** the D-039 screens and components are deleted; new app = checkpoint provider + sweep control + Scan screen (React + react-three-fiber, same stack). Colour encodes track state (blue = acquired by this sweep, white = held), not categories; isolation by car/market/channel/label/engine via the key.
- Consequences: the old API endpoints stay until the new screens replace them; their tests assume the 3-wave demo DB (3 fail on the current wave-1 DB, unrelated to this change). The calibration lab (`web/lab.html`, `web/src/three`) is kept.

## D-042 — One 5 Series; car rings carry dated public data
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("merge them into one 5 Series sector"; chose "add public July data" for the static rings), implemented by agent · Status: accepted
- Context: G68 has no comments and no own sales row (BMW's sheet is one G60_G68 tab); as its own car it was a near-empty sector. Study, options and sales rings never changed at JUL because BMW's files exist once (all known at JAN, D-041).
- Decision:
  1. **The 5 Series is one car line.** Requirements belong to the line; the China target is realised on the G68 (`market_variant`), US/EU on the G60. The G68 stays a separate vehicle in the data. On the scan: three car sectors; the last ~28 % of the 5 Series sector is the "LWB · China" part (G68 study items and sales, China research).
  2. **Car-specific public research goes onto the car's rings** (`api/routers/scan.py: research_cars / research_ring`): sales metrics → sales ring (stem = public volume), studies/reviews/awards → study ring, product news → options ring. They are contacts like the comments (dot = held, ring = acquired at JUL, flare when the sweep passes), drawn beside BMW's own marks and never blended with them (Q-015). The date ring keeps the remaining research and moved inside, next to the comments.
- Consequences: at JUL every ring gains items (public H1 2026 sales, J.D. Power 2026 IQS/APEAL awards, ADAC 2026, the 7 Series facelift and i7-China news). Matching is a regex on entity/headline; items naming BMW as a whole are matched by headline.

## D-043 — Structure & context: classify → cluster → contextualize → elicit, per checkpoint
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan (fresh extraction; evidence graph in SQLite with RAG; page 2 "collapse into structure"; "spawn sub agents to find optimizations … I want to see improvements with the new data"), designed from three read-only reviews (classification, clustering, contextualize), implemented by agent · Status: accepted
- Decision (code in `src/bmw_req/structure/`, every stage a `checkpoint_run`; cp2 builds on cp1):
  1. **classify** (`classify.py`, extract-v4): fixed ~45-aspect taxonomy shared by all sources (`taxonomy.py`); intensity (1–3) separate from impact; nature/want_kind/occupant/context/benchmark/future_cue/explicit; one signal per (aspect, nature); hints for Source C self-reported severity and the Source D survey prompt (never quoted); quotes ≥ 4 words; ~2.6k-token cacheable prompt; 20 comments per luna Flex call. cp2 classifies only the delta. A/B on a fixed 400-comment sample (`scripts/benchmark_classify.py`, `data/eval/classify_ab.json`): BMW-label macro 0.609 → 0.615, likes 0.84 → 0.90, "serious" → high 0.17 → 0.37, "minor" → low 0.22 → 0.49, quotes < 4 words 13 % → 5 %, survey-prompt quotes 10 → 0, Korea in-scope 0.71 → 0.76, aspect coverage 0 → 99 %; wants 0.56 → 0.54 (≈). `classify_context.py`: study rows (|z| ≥ 0.8 → gap/like), research (luna: aspect + nature), options (aspect) into `source_aspect`.
  2. **cluster** (`cluster.py`): portfolio-wide within polarity × category, average linkage 0.35 + recursive split of oversized clusters; stable keys `cl:<pol>:<cat>:<anchor>`; cp2 assigns new signals to cp1 clusters (mean-member cosine ≤ 0.35), clusters only leftovers; track weight = comment share, strengthened/weakened only if ≥ 10 % relative AND |z| ≥ 1.96 (the random JAN/JUL split must not look like change).
  3. **contextualize** (`contextualize.py`): luna standardizes one insight per cluster (title, statement, need type, quality issue, product decision); duplicate judge on cosine ≥ 0.86 pairs; themes (average linkage 0.45 on statement embeddings, cp2 joins nearest cp1 theme ≥ 0.55); RAG: research/study/options embedded once (`node_embedding`), per theme top-k checkpoint-visible candidates verified by luna into typed `evidence_edge`s (supports, contradicts, competes_with, trend_for, available_as_option, context). cp2 re-runs only changed clusters/themes; clean ones carry their edges as held.
  4. **areas** (`areas.py`): this step structures, it does not draft requirements (Atahan: drafting proposals is the next step). sol groups the themes into 15–40 potential requirement areas (title, need, kind improve / keep / emerging, why now from the given evidence, ≤ 3 open questions for drafting); code adds comments, line × market coverage and evidence counts; quality-only themes form a separate quality list. cp2 keeps area keys, attaches new themes, records change notes; tracks significance-tested. `elicit.py` (candidate drafting with code checks: future horizon needs a dated trend edge, own-market evidence per target, cited ids from the theme's edges) is kept for the next step and not run here.
  5. **Page 2 "Structure"** (`/structure`, same canvas as the scan): comments morph into their clusters; cluster nodes (blue improve / white keep; dot held, ring new, double ring strengthened, amber weakened/lost), theme halos, requirement-area diamonds above their themes, evidence arcs to the exact ring items; stage funnel; live agent panel (stages, progress, feed of AI steps from the audit trail; comments flash as they are classified); inspectors for clusters (signals with quotes), themes (evidence by relation) and areas (need, why now, open questions, coverage); "What the AI found" on comments and research on page 1. API `api/routers/structure.py`.
- Consequences: the old pipeline (`pipeline/`, extract-v3, findings, requirements, linker) stays for history but the new screens read only D-043 tables. Q-021 (over-linking) and the D-038 defect rule are enforced in code here.

## D-044 — App name "SharkSight" and the shark-nose logo
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("SharkSight olsun, logoyu çizip uygulamaya ekle, minimal bir logo olsun"), implemented by agent · Status: accepted · Renames the D-039 app "Successor".
- Decision: the app is called **SharkSight**: BMW's forward-leaning "shark nose" (Haifischnase, back in the Neue Klasse concepts) + foresight, because the app projects successor requirements. Pitch line: "Smaller kidneys. Sharper foresight." The logo is a great white's head seen straight from the side, abstracted to a single geometric line (dome to the snout tip, a straight mouth cut, the lower jaw), traced from a reference photo Atahan supplied (`web/src/components/Logo.tsx`, `web/public/favicon.svg`). No BMW roundel or M logo, to avoid trademark issues and to avoid looking like an official BMW product.
- Consequences: the wordmark sits left of the page tabs at top centre; the top-bar pills (Evidence, Structure, Audit) grew from 28 to 32px, 13px text, to carry it. The localStorage key `successor.actor` is kept so the saved PM actor survives the rename.

## D-045 — Audit trail separated by checkpoint; pre-rebuild history hidden, not deleted
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan asked to separate the audit trail by checkpoint and allowed erasing the rows from before the app refactor; implemented by agent · Status: accepted.
- Decision: `/api/audit/feed` shows only the selected checkpoint's rows on the Evidence and Structure scopes. "Everything" shows both checkpoints, each tagged. The classifier's A/B test is tagged `ab` (shown in Everything only). A data load that fed both checkpoints is split into one row per checkpoint with its item count. Rows from before the first checkpoint run (the old wave-based app, 1,114 events) are **not deleted**: `audit_event` is append-only by rule 6 and DB triggers. Instead the feed leaves them out unless `history=true`, which is a toggle at the end of Everything ("Show history before the checkpoint rebuild").
- Consequences: no history is lost. A physical delete would mean dropping the append-only triggers and needs an explicit PM decision. A backup of the DB and a JSON export of the pre-rebuild rows were taken anyway (`data/backups/`, git-ignored).

## D-046 — Sales in the AI pipeline: BMW's file as a labelled weight, trends from public figures, conflicts surfaced
- Date: 2026-10-11 · Decided by: Atahan ("satış verisini de AI kullansın … ama verilerin yanlışlığını teyit et"), after the sales verification (`research/sales-verification.md`, Q-015 note); implemented by agent · Status: accepted.
- Context: the verification found the ingest correct (36/36 rows match the xlsx) but BMW's market split implausible (5 Series US ≈ 3× public, China LWB 21–39 % low, 7 Series grows +24 % vs −5.6 % public; the 5 Series global total matches), and every 2024 → 2030 growth contradicts H1 2026 public declines. Clustering stays comment-only (study/research enter via the evidence graph).
- Decision (`src/bmw_req/structure/market.py`, deterministic, no LLM):
  1. **BMW's sales file = relative weight only**: share of BMW's 2025 volume per car line × market (G60 + G68 summed), always labelled "internal and stylized (Q-015)". Its growth is never used as a trend.

# Design System: SharkSight

## Overview

**Creative North Star: "Track-While-Scan"**

The whole interface is a scan volume. A true-black field holds every piece of raw evidence as a contact in one fixed 3D space; each checkpoint is a sweep that passes through that space, and the screen shows what the sweep acquired and how existing tracks changed. The 3D canvas is the page. Everythin

Density sits in the contacts, not in the text. Numerals carry the information, set wide, light and tabular like instrument readouts; words are short labels. The only running text is the customer's own words, shown in the inspector at reading size. Colour is categorical and earned: each raw data type

Motion is a single event, not ambience. The volume never turns by itself; it moves only when the PM drags it. The sweep plays once on arrival and once on each checkpoint change, and contacts it passes flare white as they are acquired.

**Key Characteristics:**
- True black ground (#000) with the live 3D canvas full-bleed behind every overlay.
- Overlays pinned to the 24px edge: readout with the filter chips under it top-left, checkpoint timeline bottom-right (both frameless), inspector top-right (frameless feathered field).
- Wide, light, tabular numerals as the primary text.
- Five categorical data-type hues, one sweep blue, amber reserved for loss.
- Mark shape encodes track state: dot = held, ring = acquired by this sweep.
- One sweep per checkpoint change; no idle motion of the volume.

## Colors

A black instrument field with white ink, five categorical data hues validated on black, and two reserved signals: sweep blue and loss amber.

### Primary
- **Sweep Blue** (sweep, sweep-hi, sweep-wash): the sweep and the PM's position. The deep step colours the sweep blade's additive wash; the bright step draws the blade's leading edge, the active checkpoint node (with a 4px sweep-wash halo), the border of a filter chip in use, a chosen filter value's

### Secondary
- **Loss Amber** (lost-amber): reserved for weakened and lost tracks, which appear from the clustering stage on. Raw sources are only ever acquired, so the scan surface uses amber only for the failed-scan message (a lost signal).

### Tertiary (categorical, one hue per raw data type)
- **Comment Blue** (type-comment): customer verbatims, the galaxy at the centre of the volume.
- **Research Vermilion** (type-research): cited web research on the dated outer ring.
- **Study Aqua** (type-study): customer-study ticks on the innermost range ring.
- **Option Ochre** (type-option): price-list equipment on the options ring.
- **Sales Magenta** (type-sales): BMW sales volumes on the sales ring; forecasts render as wireframe outlines in the same hue.

The same hue colours the data type's inline legend glyph wherever the type is named (readout, ring name tags, inspector header).

### Neutral
- **Void** (void): the page and the WebGL clear colour. Never a near-black; pure black is what makes the contacts read as emitters.
- **Smoked Glass** (glass): the page switch, with a backdrop blur over the canvas.
- **Field** (field): every other panel (inspector, hover card, filter values, audit trail, dock). Plain black at 86%, under a 10px blur and a feathered edge. No glow.
- **Hairline** (hair) and **Strong Hairline** (hair-strong): panel borders, chip outlines, filter bar tracks, the checkpoint rail, the z-bar midline, scrollbars, mobile pill outlines.
- **Ink** (ink): numerals, titles, the customer quote, active labels, the held mark.
- **Ink 2** (ink-2): secondary values, filter names and counts, ring labels, the checkpoint fill.
- **Ink 3** (ink-3): micro labels, inactive tabs and nodes, meta lines. Holds at least 4.5:1 on black; it is the floor for any text.

In 3D, range rings are white at 10% opacity and the time ring is a white dashed line at 22%.

### Named Rules
**The One Blue Rule.** Sweep blue means "the sweep, or where the PM is right now". It never fills a data series and never decorates.

**The Amber Is Loss Rule.** Amber appears only for weakened or lost tracks and lost signal. Option Ochre sits near it in hue, so a lost track always also carries its cross mark; amber never encodes state on its own.

**The White Is Attention Rule.** Contacts rest in their data-type hue. They turn white only while a sweep flares them, while hovered, or under the white lock reticle. Blue is not used for hover.

## Typography

**Display Font:** Mona Sans Variable with its width axis (fallback ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif)
**Body Font:** the same family; one family runs the whole system.

**Character:** One grotesque in two voices. Numerals are stretched wide (118%), light (300) and tabular, so counts read like instrument dials; labels are the same face at normal width, small and quiet. Tabular figures are on globally.

### Hierarchy
- **Instrument** (300, 34px, line-height 1, -0.02em, width 118%): the readout totals (28px), the inspector's key figure (34px) and the checkpoint timeline's track counts (20px). Readout drops to 22px under 760px.
- **Read** (400, 18px, line-height 1.5, max 60ch): the customer's words in the inspector; the only reading text in the system.
- **Title** (500, 18px, line-height 1.35, balanced wrap): the inspected item's name or headline.
- **Body** (400, 14px, line-height 1.45): the base size; sweep-control track counts, secondary figures.
- **Detail** (400, 13px): hover-card text (clamped to three lines), inspector fact values, the source link.
- **Label** (400 or 600, 12px): filter chips, filter values and counts, layer names, "+n" increments. At 600 with 0.08em tracking it names checkpoints (JAN 26 / JUL 26).
- **Micro** (400, 11px, 0.02em, ink-3): field and readout labels, legend names, ring sublabels; at 600 with 0.1em tracking it labels the time ring.

### Named Rules
**The Numeral Leads Rule.** Where a value exists, the numeral is the largest thing in its group and its label sits beside or above it at micro size. Labels never outrank figures.

# SharkSight — 3-minute pitch script

Open `pitch/index.html` in a browser. Use → / Space or click to advance, ← to go back, and `f` for fullscreen.
Target: about 420 spoken words, which is about 2:50. Times are cumulative.

Figures come from `data/app.db` and `foundation/` on 2026-10-11. Re-check them before the pitch, because Definition at JUL is still being generated.

---

**1 · Title (0:00–0:15)**
This is SharkSight. The shark nose is coming back with the Neue Klasse, and we pair it with foresight. Smaller kidneys, sharper foresight. SharkSight helps a BMW product manager decide what the next car must do for its customers.

**2 · Problem (0:15–0:40)**
A PM has more than ten thousand customer comments, a customer study, sales and option lists, and a market that changes every month. US, European and Chinese customers want different things. The process runs for about two years, so every decision has to stay traceable. Our app moves from evidence to structure to definition, and the PM decides at every step.

**3 · Evidence (0:40–1:05)**
Page one shows every source as one 3D scan. It holds 10,128 comments across the 1, 5 and 7 Series, BMW's study, options and sales, and almost 1,400 cited web items with a URL, a date and a trust tier. Time runs on two real checkpoints, January and July 2026, and July builds on January. We also check BMW's own sales file against public figures. When they disagree by more than 25 %, we flag the gap instead of hiding it.

**4 · Structure (1:05–1:35)**
Page two is where the AI reads. It classifies every comment into about 45 shared aspects and clusters them into 562 needs across the portfolio. Then it links those needs to research, study and competitor evidence, about nine thousand links in total. The result is about 40 requirement areas. When new data arrives, the app tests every change for statistical significance, so noise doesn't look like a trend. Defects go to Quality, not into requirements.

**5 · Definition (1:35–2:10)**
Page three answers BMW's question: "Range: 600 or 700 miles?" Each area becomes measurable requirements, 76 so far. Each one gets a metric the customer actually experiences and a target ladder for each car and market: today's BMW, rival parity, a target projected to launch, and a stretch goal. Every number is marked as cited, projected, an assumption or a gap. The numbers come from 246 cited benchmarks, and the AI never invents one. The AI recommends a rung, and the PM picks it. The requirements are linked like the roof of a House of Quality. For example, range and agility compete through mass. All of it sits on the 3D car.

**6 · Trust (2:10–2:35)**
The AI only proposes; a named person decides, and every decision needs a reason. Nothing is overwritten. Each run is a new version, and all 2,193 audit events are append-only. Every requirement links to its evidence. We have spent about 11 dollars of our 100-dollar model budget, and every call is logged.

**7 · Next (2:35–2:50)**
Next comes prioritization per market. Linked requirements are bundled, and conflicts are decided together. Let me show you live.

---

## Facts behind the slides

- Sources: 10,128 feedback, 391 study, 458 options, 24 sales rows, 1,028 research, 245 web, 96 reference items (`source_item`).

"""Build pitch/SharkSight-pitch.pptx, an editable PowerPoint copy of pitch/index.html.

Run: uv run --no-project --with python-pptx python pitch/build_pptx.py
Speaker notes come from pitch/script.md. Keep the text in sync with index.html.
"""

import re
from io import BytesIO
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.enum.text import MSO_ANCHOR, PP_ALIGN
from pptx.util import Emu, Pt

HERE = Path(__file__).parent
FONT = "Helvetica Neue"

VOID = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
INK = RGBColor(0xF2, 0xF4, 0xF7)
INK2 = RGBColor(0xB4, 0xBA, 0xC4)
INK3 = RGBColor(0x86, 0x8D, 0x99)
HAIR = RGBColor(0x2E, 0x2E, 0x2E)
SWEEP = RGBColor(0x4D, 0x94, 0xFF)
SWEEP_WASH = RGBColor(0x0A, 0x1E, 0x3A)
LOST = RGBColor(0xF5, 0xA5, 0x24)

W, H = Emu(12192000), Emu(6858000)  # 16:9
IN = 914400
LEFT = int(0.9 * IN)
CW = W - 2 * LEFT

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width, prs.slide_height = W, H
BLANK = prs.slide_layouts[6]


def text(slide, x, y, w, h, runs, size, color=INK, bold=False, light=False, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
         anchor=MSO_ANCHOR.TOP, spacing=None):
    """runs: str, or list of paragraphs; each paragraph a str or list of (text, overrides) tuples."""
    box = slide.shapes.add_textbox(x, y, w, h)
    tf = box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    tf.vertical_anchor = anchor
    for m in ("margin_left", "margin_right", "margin_top", "margin_bottom"):
        setattr(tf, m, 0)
    paras = runs if isinstance(runs, list) else [runs]
    for i, para in enumerate(paras):
        p = tf.paragraphs[0] if i == 0 else tf.add_paragraph()
        p.alignment = align
        if spacing:
            p.space_after = Pt(spacing)
        for t, o in ([(para, {})] if isinstance(para, str) else para):
            r = p.add_run()
            r.text = t
            f = r.font
            f.name = FONT + (" Light" if o.get("light", light) else "")
            f.size = Pt(o.get("size", size))
            f.bold = o.get("bold", bold)
            f.color.rgb = o.get("color", color)
    return box


def chrome(slide, n, total):
    slide.background.fill.solid()
    slide.background.fill.fore_color.rgb = VOID
    text(slide, LEFT, H - int(0.5 * IN), CW, int(0.25 * IN),
         "SharkSight · BMW AI for Product Decision Making · EHL – Grand Finale", 10, INK3)
    text(slide, LEFT, H - int(0.5 * IN), CW, int(0.25 * IN), f"{n} / {total}", 10, INK3, align=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)
    bar = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, H - Emu(25400), int(W * n / total), Emu(25400))
    bar.fill.solid()
    bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = SWEEP
    bar.line.fill.background()


def kicker(slide, y, label):
    text(slide, LEFT, y, CW, int(0.3 * IN), label.upper(), 12, SWEEP, bold=True)


def heading(slide, y, t, h=int(1.3 * IN), size=36):
    text(slide, LEFT, y, int(CW * 0.85), h, t, size, INK)


def bullets(slide, y, items, w=int(CW * 0.8), size=18):
    paras = [[("○  ", {"color": SWEEP}), (b, {"bold": True, "color": INK}), (" " + r, {"color": INK2})] for b, r in items]
    return text(slide, LEFT, y, w, int(0.5 * IN) * len(items), paras, size, spacing=10)


def flow(slide, y, steps, current):
    x = LEFT
    for i, s in enumerate(steps):
        w = int((0.22 + 0.105 * len(s)) * IN)
        pill = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, x, y, w, int(0.45 * IN))
        pill.adjustments[0] = 0.5
        pill.fill.background()
        pill.line.color.rgb = SWEEP if s == current else HAIR
        pill.line.width = Pt(1)
        tf = pill.text_frame
        tf.margin_left = tf.margin_right = 0
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
        r = p.add_run()
        r.text = s
        r.font.name, r.font.size = FONT, Pt(15)
        r.font.color.rgb = INK if s == current else INK2
        x += w
        if i < len(steps) - 1:
            text(slide, x, y, int(0.4 * IN), int(0.45 * IN), "→", 15, INK3, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER, anchor=MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE)
            x += int(0.4 * IN)


def rule(slide, y, w=CW):
    ln = slide.shapes.add_connector(1, LEFT, y, LEFT + w, y)
    ln.line.color.rgb = HAIR
    ln.line.width = Pt(1)


def columns(slide, y, cols, big=34, small=13, w=CW, pick=None):
    rule(slide, y, w)
    cw = w // len(cols)
    for i, (b, s) in enumerate(cols):
        text(slide, LEFT + i * cw, y + int(0.25 * IN), cw - int(0.2 * IN), int(1.4 * IN),
             [[(b, {"size": big, "light": big > 24, "color": SWEEP if b == pick else INK})], [(s, {"color": INK3})]],
             small, spacing=6)


def logo(slide, x, y, size):
    slide.shapes.add_picture(str(HERE / "assets/logo.png"), x, y, size, size)


def round_photo(path, px=600, zoom=1.08):
    im = Image.open(path).convert("RGB")
    s = min(im.size)
    c = int(s / zoom)
    l, t = (im.width - c) // 2, (im.height - c) // 2
    im = im.crop((l, t, l + c, t + c)).resize((px, px), Image.LANCZOS)
    mask = Image.new("L", (px, px), 0)
    ImageDraw.Draw(mask).ellipse((0, 0, px - 1, px - 1), fill=255)
    out = Image.new("RGBA", (px, px))
    out.paste(im, (0, 0), mask)
    buf = BytesIO()
    out.save(buf, "PNG")
    buf.seek(0)
    return buf


def notes_from_script():
    src = (HERE / "script.md").read_text()
    blocks = re.findall(r"\*\*(\d+) · [^*]+\*\*\n(.+?)(?=\n\n|\Z)", src, re.S)
    return {int(n): body.strip() for n, body in blocks}


SLIDES = []


def slide(fn):
    SLIDES.append(fn)
    return fn


@slide
def title(s):
    logo(s, LEFT - int(0.15 * IN), int(1.35 * IN), int(1.3 * IN))
    text(s, LEFT + int(1.3 * IN), int(1.45 * IN), CW, int(1.2 * IN), "SharkSight", 80, light=True)
    text(s, LEFT, int(2.95 * IN), CW, int(1.6 * IN), ["Solid evidence.", "Sound decisions."], 40)
    text(s, LEFT, int(4.75 * IN), int(CW * 0.7), int(1 * IN),
         "A broad knowledge base built from thousands of raw data points. The AI structures it. "
         "The PM decides what the next BMW must deliver.", 20, INK2)


@slide
def team(s):
    kicker(s, int(0.9 * IN), "The team")
    heading(s, int(1.25 * IN), "Zimbabwe", size=40)
    d = int(2.3 * IN)
    cw = int(3.6 * IN)
    x0 = (W - 3 * cw) // 2
    y = int(2.85 * IN)
    people = [("Musa Berkay Kocabaşoğlu", False), ("Atahan Kılıç", True), ("Utku Kalkanlı", False)]
    for i, (name, me) in enumerate(people):
        cx = x0 + i * cw + cw // 2
        if me:
            halo = s.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, cx - d // 2 - Emu(76200), y - Emu(76200), d + Emu(152400), d + Emu(152400))
            halo.fill.solid()
            halo.fill.fore_color.rgb = SWEEP_WASH
            halo.line.fill.background()
            s.shapes.add_picture(round_photo(HERE / "assets/atahan.png"), cx - d // 2, y, d, d)
            ring = s.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, cx - d // 2, y, d, d)
            ring.fill.background()
            ring.line.color.rgb = SWEEP
            ring.line.width = Pt(2)
        else:
            text(s, cx - cw // 2, y - int(0.45 * IN), cw, int(0.35 * IN), "✕ Missing", 16, LOST, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
            o = s.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, cx - d // 2, y, d, d)
            o.fill.background()
            o.line.color.rgb = LOST
            o.line.width = Pt(2)
            o.line.dash_style = 4  # dash
            text(s, cx - d // 2, y, d, d, "?", 60, INK3, light=True, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER, anchor=MSO_ANCHOR.MIDDLE)
        text(s, cx - cw // 2, y + d + int(0.2 * IN), cw, int(0.4 * IN), name, 20,
             INK if me else INK3, bold=me, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)


@slide
def problem(s):
    kicker(s, int(1.0 * IN), "The problem")
    heading(s, int(1.4 * IN), "Thousands of customer voices. Many markets. One question: what must the successor do?")
    bullets(s, int(3.0 * IN), [
        ("Evidence is scattered:", "verbatims, customer studies, sales and option lists, plus a fast-moving market."),
        ("Markets are different customers:", "the US, Europe and China must not be averaged away."),
        ("Decisions live for years:", "new evidence keeps arriving, and every decision has to stay traceable."),
    ])
    flow(s, int(5.15 * IN), ["Evidence", "Structure", "Definition", "PM decision"], "Evidence")


@slide
def evidence(s):
    kicker(s, int(1.0 * IN), "Evidence")
    heading(s, int(1.4 * IN), "Every source in one space, always live.", h=int(0.8 * IN))
    columns(s, int(2.55 * IN), [
        ("Voice", "what customers say,\nacross car lines"),
        ("Data", "BMW studies, options\nand sales"),
        ("World", "cited web research with\nsource, date and trust"),
        ("Live", "new data keeps flowing in;\nevery update builds on the last"),
    ])
    bullets(s, int(4.65 * IN), [
        ("Honest data:", "internal figures are checked against public ones, and conflicts are shown, never blended silently."),
    ])


@slide
def structure(s):
    kicker(s, int(1.0 * IN), "Structure")
    heading(s, int(1.4 * IN), "The AI reads everything and builds an evidence graph.", h=int(0.8 * IN))
    flow(s, int(2.5 * IN), ["Classify", "Cluster", "Contextualize", "Requirement areas"], "Requirement areas")
    bullets(s, int(3.45 * IN), [
        ("One shared language", "for comments, studies and research, across the whole portfolio."),
        ("Needs are linked to the world:", "what supports them, what contradicts them, and where rivals compete."),
        ("Change is tested statistically,", "so new data can't fake a trend. Defects go to Quality, not into requirements."),
    ])


@slide
def definition(s):
    kicker(s, int(1.0 * IN), "Definition")
    heading(s, int(1.4 * IN), "From need to a measurable requirement, placed on the car.", h=int(0.8 * IN))
    columns(s, int(2.45 * IN), [
        ("Baseline", "today's BMW"), ("Threshold", "rival parity"),
        ("Target", "projected to launch"), ("Stretch", "delighter"),
    ], big=20, small=14, w=int(CW * 0.75), pick="Target")
    bullets(s, int(3.65 * IN), [
        ("One metric the customer feels,", "with a target ladder per car and market. The AI recommends a rung; the PM picks."),
        ("Every number has a basis:", "cited, projected, assumption or gap. The AI never invents a number to fill a gap."),
        ("Requirements are linked,", "like the roof of a House of Quality. Example: range ↔ agility, via mass."),
    ])


@slide
def trust(s):
    kicker(s, int(1.0 * IN), "Built for trust")
    heading(s, int(1.4 * IN), "The AI proposes. The PM decides. Everything is on record.")
    bullets(s, int(3.05 * IN), [
        ("Every requirement traces back", "to the evidence behind it."),
        ("Every decision is audited,", "append-only, with who decided and why."),
        ("Nothing is overwritten:", "each run is a new version, linked to the one before."),
        ("Every model call is logged", "by step and cost."),
    ])


@slide
def vision(s):
    kicker(s, int(1.3 * IN), "The vision")
    heading(s, int(1.7 * IN), "A product brain that keeps learning, across every car line and market.")
    text(s, LEFT, int(3.3 * IN), int(CW * 0.7), int(0.9 * IN),
         "Next: prioritization per market, where linked requirements are bundled and conflicts are decided together.", 20, INK2)
    logo(s, LEFT - int(0.1 * IN), int(4.45 * IN), int(0.75 * IN))
    text(s, LEFT + int(0.75 * IN), int(4.55 * IN), CW, int(0.6 * IN), "SharkSight · Live demo →", 26, light=True)


notes = notes_from_script()
for i, build in enumerate(SLIDES, 1):
    s = prs.slides.add_slide(BLANK)
    chrome(s, i, len(SLIDES))
    build(s)
    if i in notes:
        s.notes_slide.notes_text_frame.text = notes[i]

I fixed the PowerPoint and reopened it. Earlier I hadn't checked the PowerPoint output; this time I exported it to PDF from PowerPoint and looked at the slides. Slides 3–6 are fine now; I made one more small spacing fix on slide 6 after that check and didn't look at it again.

- **Overlapping text:** On slides 3, 5 and 6 the long headings ran into the text below. Headings now use the full slide width and the content starts lower.
- **Bullets:** When a bullet ran onto a second line, that line started under the dot. Wrapped lines now line up with the text.
- **The "↔" arrow:** PowerPoint showed it as an emoji, so it now reads "range vs. agility, via mass". I made the same change in the web deck.

To reopen the deck, I closed every open PowerPoint window without saving. If you had another presentation open with unsaved changes, those changes are lost, sorry.

Python 3.12, uv, OpenAI API (GPT models + text-embedding-3-small), LangGraph, SQLite, sqlite-vec, scikit-learn, Pydantic, FastAPI, Uvicorn, React, TypeScript, Vite, three.js, React Three Fiber, TanStack Query, Motion, pytest
